title: Prediction: Colette Kress Is More Vital to Nvidia’s Future Than Her Interim CEO Title Implies
author: Daniel Foelber
description: Following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO due to personal scandals, CFO Colette Kress has assumed the interim CEO role. The article argues that Kress, who has historically balanced Huang's visionary but risky bets with financial discipline, may fundamentally shift Nvidia's strategy toward a more cautious approach. This could slow growth but reduce vulnerability to AI spending downturns, potentially transforming Nvidia from a high-growth stock into a value-oriented investment.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the leadership transition creates uncertainty and near-term volatility, the article suggests Kress's more disciplined approach could benefit long-term investors by reducing risky bets and maintaining high margins. The stock is down significantly, but the fundamental business remains strong with potential for steady compounding rather than boom-bust cycles.

title: Eaton vs. Corning: Which Industrials Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: The article compares Eaton Corp. and Corning Inc. as potential industrial stock investments for 2027. Eaton, with 10% revenue growth and a lower P/E ratio of 33.67, benefits from electrification and data center trends with strong order backlogs. Corning, showing 19% revenue growth and ambitious plans to reach $40 billion in sales by 2030 through AI data center deals, trades at a premium P/E of 43.06 but offers greater long-term growth potential. The author ultimately favors Corning for 2027 despite its higher valuation.

title: Broadcom vs. Micron Technology: Which Tech Stock Is the Better Buy for 2027?
author: John Ballard
description: Both Broadcom and Micron Technology are benefiting from the AI boom, but they operate in different segments. Broadcom designs custom chips and software for networking and storage with strong long-term growth prospects, while Micron specializes in memory products with impressive current profits but vulnerability to price swings. The author recommends Broadcom for 2027 due to more stable earnings growth and lower long-term risk, despite Micron's cheaper valuation metrics.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better buy for 2027 due to custom AI chip design capabilities, strong free cash flow ($39B), improving forward P/E ratio (11x by fiscal 2028), and more stable long-term earnings growth compared to competitors. Lower customer concentration risk relative to memory-dependent businesses.

While showing impressive current financial metrics (256% revenue growth, $85B net income, strong balance sheet with 0.0x debt-to-equity), the stock is considered riskier long-term due to vulnerability to memory price swings, intense competition from Samsung and SK Hynix, and historical financial volatility. Cheaper valuation (3.9x forward P/E) is offset by cyclical business risks.
Mentioned as a major long-term customer of Broadcom's custom chips, indicating stable business relationships but also highlighting Broadcom's customer concentration risk.

title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 17: Stocks Slide on AI Chip and Tech Pressures, Salesforce Plummets 9%
author: Emma Newbery
description: Major stock indexes fell for the fourth consecutive day on November 17, 2026, as AI concerns and technology outages weighed on investor confidence. The S&P 500 dropped 1.03%, the Nasdaq fell 0.74%, and the Dow Jones declined 1.64%. Salesforce plummeted 9.45% amid security concerns and AI replacement fears. However, Nvidia's after-hours earnings beat expectations, offering some reassurance on AI infrastructure demand.

title: Warren Buffett’s Successor, Greg Abel, Has 30.2% of Berkshire’s $367 Billion Portfolio in Just 2 Magnificent Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks. Here’s the One I’d Buy Without Hesitation.
author: Adam Spatacco
description: Berkshire Hathaway has concentrated nearly 30% of its $367 billion stock portfolio in two AI-exposed stocks: Apple (21.9%) and Alphabet (8.3%). While both companies align with Buffett's investment philosophy of durable competitive advantages, the article argues Apple is the more defensive long-term buy due to its ecosystem, customer loyalty, and recurring services revenue, whereas Alphabet's aggressive AI infrastructure investments introduce greater risk despite offering more direct AI exposure.
